before_ingredients_html:
Simplified version

Buy a small, ready-trimmed raw-use loin; slice and serve with the dip only. This simplifies preparation, never supplier checks or cold storage. If raw-use controls cannot be verified, choose a cooked fish recipe using properly cold-held fish.

notes.html:
• Raw seafood retains bacterial risk even after parasite controls.
  • Pregnant people, young children, older adults and people with weakened immunity should choose fully cooked seafood.

• Make the core ingredient list first.
  • Optional additions are separate; each is called out where it enters.
  • Quantities serve two.
  • Cook meat and seafood just before eating; keep dairy and raw ingredients refrigerated at 0–4 °C.
  • Prep vegetables before raw meat or use a separate board and clean tools.

steps.body_html:
• Confirm exact species, raw-consumption suitability and parasite-control documentation with the supplier.
  • Keep sealed at 0–4 °C, transport on ice and prepare on purchase day.
  • Thaw frozen seafood in the fridge following its label; remove keep-frozen vacuum-packed fish from its packaging before thawing.
  • No room-temperature thawing.
steps.title: Verify and chill

steps.body_html:
• Stir soy, lemon and water in a small cup.
  • Keep the dip separate until eating.
  • Wash hands and use a freshly cleaned board, sharp long knife and chilled plate.
  • Slice optional cucumber into 2 mm rounds on a separate clean board before handling seafood.
  • Work with one small portion at a time, leaving the rest refrigerated.

images.alt: Mix the dip; prepare clean tools

steps.title: Mix the dip; prepare clean tools

steps.body_html:
• Pat the seafood dry with clean disposable paper.
  • For a trimmed tuna or salmon loin, find the direction of the visible muscle lines and cut across them into 5–7 mm slices.
  • Use one long pulling stroke per slice, without sawing.
  • Keep the guiding hand well behind the blade; do not attempt to slice a slippery tiny offcut.
  • See the species notes below for scallops and specialist alternatives.
steps.title: Slice across the grain

steps.body_html:
• Arrange 150 g seafood per person in one layer.
  • Add optional cucumber; serve the dip beside it.
  • Mandarin may replace lemon; olive oil and chilli are optional additions to the dip.
  • Do not leave a communal platter in the sun.
  • Lemon, soy, quick searing and a boat freezer do not replace raw-use controls.
  • Reject seafood after a failed cold chain; cooking cannot rescue it.
steps.title: Plate cold; eat immediately
